clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 9830, Part III, revokes the listed Executive orders including "No. 8937 of November 7, 1941." The enacting clause orders EO 9830 "it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:" so the end is recorded as 1947-05-01. Part III has no separate date and the enacting clause orders Parts I, II and III alike 'effective May 1, 1947'; the alternative reading is that the revocation took effect on signing, 1947-02-24 (printed 12 FR 1259, 1947-02-25). Later event (amendment, clause continues as amended): EO 9579 restated the proviso, effective as of December 8, 1944 ("This order shall be effective as of December 8, 1944."). Before: "Provided, that such persons shall notify the Civil Service Commission within forty days after their service in the armed forces has terminated that they desire to have the benefits of this order." After: "Provided, That such persons shall notify the Civil Service Commission within 90 days after termination of their service in the armed forces or of hospitalization continuing after discharge for a period of not more than one year." The change lengthens the notice period and adds hospitalization; the substance of the proviso changed.

research_rationale:
Identity and text: read in full in the registered Federal Register original (6 FR 5708, issue of 1941-11-11, PDF page 2; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Order 8937 of November 7, 1941, 'Extending the Period of Eligibility on Civil Service Registers or Lists of Persons Who Serve in the Armed Forces of the United States', provides that service after May 1, 1940 is not counted in determining eligibility period, with a proviso on notice to the Commission, and supersedes Executive Order No. 8602. Inventory: one sole paragraph. Later event: EO 9579 (signed June 30, 1945, held APP transcription, page check done) restates the proviso, effective as of December 8, 1944. End: EO 9830, Part III (official Federal Register text, 12 FR 1259, held with its PDF) revokes the listed orders including "No. 8937 of November 7, 1941." The dossier had no ACT record for this pair; the naming is supplied as the held excerpt SUPPLEMENT:FR9830P3 and the enacting clause as SUPPLEMENT:FR9830ENACT.

savings.reason: EO 9830 Rule II section 2.1(b) independently provides that "the names of persons who lost eligibility on a probational register because of service in the armed forces subsequent to May 1, 1940" may be entered on registers, an independent command covering the persons EO 8937 protected. EO 9830 has no savings wording for revoked orders.
